newsitem.title: UK: ONS says big bonuses push up UK Jan avg earnings.
newsitem.headline: ONS says big bonuses push up UK Jan avg earnings.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics said the jump in underlying average earnings in January to 5.0 percent was largely due to bonuses in the service sector.
January is not typically a month in which bonuses are paid.
The ONS added the big upward revision in December's average earnings figures, to 4.75 percent from 4.25 at the original estimate, was also due to higher pay in the service sector.
The unemployment numbers continued to be affected by distortions following the introduction of the Jobseekers Allowance last October.
"Nevertheless, the recorded unemployment falls sustained over the last six months suggest that the rate of fall in unemployment is now higher than it was in mid-1996," the ONS said.
The distortions relate to changes in operational procedures in the benefit regime itself and labour market behaviour.
The ONS said it is not possible to adjust the statistics fully for all these effects.
